Is South Africa's housing market dying?

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South Africa's property market is in the doldrums, is it time to change the way we fundamentally think about property creating wealth

Unique Selling Point:
A consumer story that directly impacts on the life and the wealth or loss of it of our viewers and gives them the latest information from the experts

Summary:
Across the board South Africans are losing money when they sell their homes. How bad is the situation. What should you do. Is there any light at the end of the tunnel and can you still make money in property, or should you just abandon this asset class for the next decade?

Further information:
Home owners desperate to sell their properties are caught in a trap. Right now, the property market is the worst it’s been for years, and for middle class South Africans some homes have taken up to three years to sell.

“When people come to me, they know I will tell it to them straight” says Jonathan Broekman from Homes of Distinction.

“I say to sellers please sit down and make yourself a cup of tea, because you aren’t going to like what I tell you. We can sell your house but if you bought it four or five years ago and you want to get your money back including transfer fees and commission, that isn’t going to happen. We might, if you are lucky get what you paid for it, but not more”

Broekman’s advice to sellers is if they don’t have to sell right now, then don’t, because if they bought at the top of the market, they will not recoup their investments.

“The housing market has been killed by taxes and it’s better to rent” says outspoken investment advisor Magnus Heystek. Recently he posted on twitter that he owns some property in Brits: “worst investment ever. I cannot sell or give away yet have to pay bond, levies and taxes. It’s a money trap and it is happening all over South Africa.”

Heystek’s time line went crazy – “It’s the same on the north coast of KZN” was one response. Another from a realtor in Cape Town who complained: Can’t sell the R6 million-rand properties even on the Atlantic Seaboard. “I have just lost R230 000 on my home in Sunninghill’ was another.

So, is the property market dead? Is the advice we got from our parents that property will always appreciate now just wrong?

“Renting is by far the better option says Heystek. We have been brainwashed to always buy property, but property has not shown any real growth for 13 years now.

12 years ago, banks were plying customers with loans. Competition to buy second properties as investments was so competitive, properties could go in a day. But those days are long gone, because a recent report tells us that even buy to let is dying. Now landlords are having to drop rents or risk losing tenants.

Kobus Lamprecht head of research at Rode and Associates says the percentage of flats standing empty in Cape Town surged from around 2% to over 8% at the beginning of this year. In Johannesburg it’s not as marked going from 3% to 7%

The latest figures show that average rentals actually fell in both Limpopo, down by 4% and North West – down by 1%. If you want to live cheaply North West is your place – where you can rent for under R5000 per month. But then of course none of the municipalities in North West got a clean audit so you might not get water and electricity and still pay rates through the nose.

So, what is going on with property. Should you just sell your home, rent, and take the rest of your money offshore. That is what some people are doing. They have downsized and are investing all their remaining funds offshore.

Many others are emigrating. Consider this- according to the latest wealth report, three thousand-dollar millionaires, left South Africa recently. That just wiped out R45 billion rand from the economy. No wonder there is a glut of houses on the market.

Estate Agents will always talk up the market, but what does the data tell us? To answer that question, we approached Lightstone. They analyse housing data down to the latest prices paid per suburb and they can show you exactly what is going on in the market. Take a look at their graphs and all the lines are going downhill. Even in Cape Town that enjoyed 12% inflation on house prices – the trends are the same.

It sounds counter intuitive to talk about house price inflation- but the higher the number the better for you as a seller, so for example- if you had bought in the Cape in the early 2000’s and sold in 2014 you would have made a killing. Not anymore. R15 million-rand homes are just not selling as foreigners exit the market, transfer costs strangle sales and visa regulations make it difficult for foreigners to enter and exit the market. Take the transfer duty of 13% on a R10 million-rand home – just like that you have added another R130 000000 to the price tag.

So, is there anywhere in South Africa where the property market can work for you? Yes, but it may not be what you want to hear. Lightstone’s graphs show an incredible return for properties under a million rand. Say to investors they should put their money into Hillbrow or Johannesburg’s inner city and they will fall about laughing. But that is where you might just get the best returns, either that or Umhlanga and Durban that has been showing the best returns.

So much so that a big home with a sea view on the South Coast won’t sell for much more than R1.5 million in Leisure Bay. That same home in Umhlanga will net you R5 million. But sorry for you if you bought land on the South Coast at R400 000 now says the agent I won’t even be able to get you R150 000.

In a light hearted but informative insert – we speak to the winners and the losers in the property market and tell you how best to navigate a difficult market, using the best and latest research.

HOME SALES FINAL SCRIPT TX SUNDAY 4TH AUGUST 2019 DURATION TEN MINUTES

Commentary One
This is Mooikloof Equestrian Estate on the Eastern Side of Pretoria, if you are looking for peace and quiet, great security and a selection of mansions to choose from, this is a good place to start.

Here you can buy your very own French Chateau with a fire place in all eight bedrooms. For R34 million it could be yours. Far more modest, is this home on sale for around R9 million rand. Owners Gillian and Dolf Grobler have had it on the market for over a year.

Gillian
We have had numerous buyers come through the premises and yes, it’s been quite difficult.

Commentary Two
It has a tennis court, river frontage and offers 980 square metres of luxury home. With two boys who will soon be out the home, they want to downsize. But buyers in this market who can afford close to a million rand in transfer fees and a 30% deposit are hard to find

Gillian
We have spent about a million rand on the property – so we would like to get about at least R8.5 in our pockets
Derek
Will you get it?
Gillian
I am positive we will get it. We have dropped our price – by R500 000 and we dropped it again this month.

LINK
It’s not easy to accept that your house may not have appreciated over the last 3 to 4 years, but in some cases, sellers are having to bite the bullet with a drop of 20 to 30 % of the price that they were gunning for

Commentary Three
Prices are tumbling across the major metro’s, only Ethekwini Municipality has bucked the downward trend. And here on the banks of the Hartebeesboort dam near Brits good returns have been largely destroyed by bad governance. Outspoken investment advisor Magnus Heystek.

Derek
Magnus your property in Brits you say your worst investment ever?
Magnus
At the height of the property boom, 2008 I was convinced to buy a property overlooking HB dam, banks gave you bond immediately and off we went. Since then its turned into a disaster – can’t sell the property, you still have to pay the bond, the rates and taxes



Commentary Four
He was so frustrated about what’s happened to our property market he turned to social media.
Derek
You tweeted about your Brits property, and you got a huge response from around the country?
Magnus
A phenomenal response and from hundreds of people saying yes, I am in the same position. Bought at the peak and they can’t sell

Commentary five
Respected reports like the FNB property barometer, and the Rode Report tell the same story, residential property is in dire- straits. And here at Lightstone where they analyse deeds data, analytics director Paul- Roux De Kok says house price growth is actually negative in real terms

Derek
It would depend on the area. But if I'd bought a house for say a million rand three years ago what could I sell it for now?
Paul
At the national house price growth as it has been over the last three years you would have probably been able to sell it for around a R1 million and eighty thousand
Derek
If I'm lucky?
Paul
If you get a buyer
Derek
that's not really showing any growth is it?
Paul
Ya, if you compare that with CPI, that means that in real terms you would have been better off just investing it in a money market account.

Commentary Six
Lightstone’ stats show there are 6.7 million properties in South Africa worth R5.5 trillion rand. Surprisingly, half of those properties are valued at R500 000 and below. In Johannesburg, Soweto is the best performing sub region while prices in Sandton are falling.

Jonathan Broekman
Prices are dropping. They're not going to pick up anytime soon, so all the more reason to list correctly to begin with

Commentary Seven
Jonathan Broekman is known as a straight- talking agent. He concentrates on the upper end of the market from Hyde Park down the William Nicol all the way to Lonehill



Jonathan
So, we are selling houses for less than we sold to those same sellers five years ago.
Derek
Five years ago?
Jonathan
Ja, which I think in real terms is about a 20 to 30 % drop overall.
Derek
Can you give us examples here of how much some investors have lost?
Jonathan
A house that we sold in the past two weeks, the seller paid six million four years ago, and we just sold for R5.8. million

DEREK LINK
It’s the age- old formula, buy property to secure your future wealth, but with prices in decline we may have to rethink property as an investment

Magnus
Property has not been a great investment for 11 years now, in fact if you adjust property prices for inflation, the average property price in SA where there are transactions is down about 23%
Derek
I am looking for some light at the end of the tunnel Magnus and I am not seeing it?
Magnus
Economic growth and confidence, if you get those two factors, I think there is a massive pent up demand from young people who want to buy but they need a signal from government that I can commit myself to 20 years of bond repayments- and they will come flooding back to the market.

Commentary eight
Instead wealthy investors prefer homes in places like Mauritius. And even property companies, say Money web, are taking flight, investing R68 billion rand overseas, last year

Hardest hit is the luxury market, which is growing at only 0.5% according to Lightstone- so if you’re looking for huge bargains, Houghton in Johannesburg, and the Atlantic Seaboard in Cape Town is where you will find them.

This home came on the market for R65 million and sold recently for R38 million rand less
for R27 million. Time to buy, says top Cape agent Denise Dogon, via skype.

Denise Dogon
So that's the kind of opportunities that I am a saying are available

Commentary nine
According to the Rode report Cape Town prices have risen 108% over the last ten years, but now house prices are slowing down, there drastically.

Derek
Denise The V and A waterfront. You were saying that turnover of sales there has decreased by what percentage?
Denise
Well according to Prop Stats there have been two confirmed sales from the beginning of the year, which is probably representing an 80 percent drop

Commentary ten
Dogon says that the drought and politics has been a huge deterrent. There are also reports of visa regulations which made it difficult for foreigners

Denise
The foreigners just don't have an appetite to buy at the moment.
Derek
Those three words Denise, expropriation without compensation. What effect do they have?
Denise
They had an effect initially when it was discussed, but it doesn't seem to be a factor that anyone's talking about at the moment.

Derek link
But it’s not all gloom and doom, we may talk about the property market being depressed but there is a sector that is surviving even thriving – like here in Cosmo City

Commentary eleven
Two years ago, Thabang Mokone and Lindiwe Mabena opened their real estate franchise in Cosmo City, a new residential area close to Lanseria airport. They haven’t looked back

Derek
What have your sales like been like over the last year?
Thabang Mokone
They have been fast, they have been everything that you can wish for in real estate

Commentary eleven
Here in Cosmo City, the average selling price is R600 000

Thabang
For R600 000 you are looking at a forty square metre house. It will be two bedrooms, one bath, dining room and kitchen

Commentary twelve
And these small homes have given investors fantastic returns says his business partner
Lindiwe Mabena

Derek
What sort of returns have buyers seen over the last five years?
Lindiwe
Five years, oh my God this area is something else. Five years back this type of house for sale for R243 000 now you can buy for R650 to R700 000
Derek
Have you invested in the market yourself?
Lindiwe
Yo! I bought my first property in Cosmo city in 2009. It’s a low- cost house so we bought it for R183 000. Whenever we are able, I still buy property in Cosmo. At the moment I have four houses
Derek
Four houses and getting good rentals?
Lindiwe
Very much so
The one that I bought for R183 it’s got cottages, so out of that I make R14 000 per month– I don’t owe that house so it pays for my house including my groceries and child school fees. The second one there’s two cottages, from that one, we are making R15 000 per month
Derek
WOW
Lindiwe
Then my bond is R4800.
Derek
Those are amazing returns
Lindiwe
Yes! you should have bought a house here Derek!
Derek
You should have told me
Lindiwe
There is still chance, you can still buy Derek!

Commentary thirteen
Its good advice, homes around R400 000 have shown 16% growth. Meanwhile, people like Broekman are buying up bargains

DEREK
What should those investors look for if buying a property in this market?
JONATHAN:
The days of owning a big property on a big piece of ground are over.
Derek
So, a well-run housing estate can still be a fair investment?
JONATHAN
Cluster houses town houses townhouses community schemes estates are evergreens. That's where we're going to be living in the future

THE END

PROMO ONE
House prices are tumbling across most South African metro’s but there are bargains out there for buyers.
Jonathan
So, we are selling houses for less than we sold to those same sellers five years ago.

PROMO TWO
For Sale, for sale! As thousands of properties come on the market, South African homes are losing value
JONATHAN:
The days of owning a big property on a big piece of ground are over.

PROMO THREE
Are you struggling to sell your home? Who are the winners and losers in our current property market?
Lindiwe
At the moment I have four houses
Derek
Four houses and getting good rentals?
Lindiwe

This home came on the market for R65 million and sold recently for R38 million rand less for R27 million. Time to buy, says top Cape agent Denise Dogon, via skype. Denise Dogon So that's the kind of opportunities that I am a saying are available Commentary nine According to the Rode report Cape Town prices have risen 108% over the last ten years, but now house prices are slowing down, there drastically. Derek Denise The V and A waterfront. You were saying that turnover of sales there has decreased by what percentage? Denise Well according to Prop Stats there have been two confirmed sales from the beginning of the year, which is probably representing an 80 percent drop Commentary ten Dogon says that the drought and politics has been a huge deterrent. There are also reports of visa regulations which made it difficult for foreigners Denise The foreigners just don't have an appetite to buy at the moment. Derek Those three words Denise, expropriation without compensation. What effect do they have? Denise They had an effect initially when it was discussed, but it doesn't seem to be a factor that anyone's talking about at the moment. Derek link But it’s not all gloom and doom, we may talk about the property market being depressed but there is a sector that is surviving even thriving – like here in Cosmo City Commentary eleven Two years ago, Thabang Mokone and Lindiwe Mabena opened their real estate franchise in Cosmo City, a new residential area close to Lanseria airport. They haven’t looked back Derek What have your sales like been like over the last year? Thabang Mokone They have been fast, they have been everything that you can wish for in real estate Commentary eleven Here in Cosmo City, the average selling price is R600 000 Thabang For R600 000 you are looking at a forty square metre house. It will be two bedrooms, one bath, dining room and kitchen Commentary twelve And these small homes have given investors fantastic returns says his business partner Lindiwe Mabena Derek What sort of returns have buyers seen over the last five years? Lindiwe Five years, oh my God this area is something else. Five years back this type of house for sale for R243 000 now you can buy for R650 to R700 000 Derek Have you invested in the market yourself? Lindiwe Yo! I bought my first property in Cosmo city in 2009. It’s a low- cost house so we bought it for R183 000. Whenever we are able, I still buy property in Cosmo. At the moment I have four houses Derek Four houses and getting good rentals? Lindiwe Very much so The one that I bought for R183 it’s got cottages, so out of that I make R14 000 per month– I don’t owe that house so it pays for my house including my groceries and child school fees. The second one there’s two cottages, from that one, we are making R15 000 per month Derek WOW Lindiwe Then my bond is R4800. Derek Those are amazing returns Lindiwe Yes! you should have bought a house here Derek! Derek You should have told me Lindiwe There is still chance, you can still buy Derek! Commentary thirteen Its good advice, homes around R400 000 have shown 16% growth. Meanwhile, people like Broekman are buying up bargains DEREK What should those investors look for if buying a property in this market? JONATHAN: The days of owning a big property on a big piece of ground are over. Derek So, a well-run housing estate can still be a fair investment? JONATHAN Cluster houses town houses townhouses community schemes estates are evergreens. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): South Africa's property market is in the doldrums, is it time to change the way we fundamentally think about property creating wealth
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A consumer story that directly impacts on the life and the wealth or loss of it of our viewers and gives them the latest information from the experts
metadata.Summary: Across the board South Africans are losing money when they sell their homes. How bad is the situation. What should you do. Is there any light at the end of the tunnel and can you still make money in property, or should you just abandon this asset class for the next decade?
metadata.Further information: Home owners desperate to sell their properties are caught in a trap. Right now, the property market is the worst it’s been for years, and for middle class South Africans some homes have taken up to three years to sell. “When people come to me, they know I will tell it to them straight” says Jonathan Broekman from Homes of Distinction. “I say to sellers please sit down and make yourself a cup of tea, because you aren’t going to like what I tell you. We can sell your house but if you bought it four or five years ago and you want to get your money back including transfer fees and commission, that isn’t going to happen. We might, if you are lucky get what you paid for it, but not more” Broekman’s advice to sellers is if they don’t have to sell right now, then don’t, because if they bought at the top of the market, they will not recoup their investments. “The housing market has been killed by taxes and it’s better to rent” says outspoken investment advisor Magnus Heystek. Recently he posted on twitter that he owns some property in Brits: “worst investment ever. I cannot sell or give away yet have to pay bond, levies and taxes. It’s a money trap and it is happening all over South Africa.” Heystek’s time line went crazy – “It’s the same on the north coast of KZN” was one response. Another from a realtor in Cape Town who complained: Can’t sell the R6 million-rand properties even on the Atlantic Seaboard. “I have just lost R230 000 on my home in Sunninghill’ was another. So, is the property market dead? Is the advice we got from our parents that property will always appreciate now just wrong? “Renting is by far the better option says Heystek. We have been brainwashed to always buy property, but property has not shown any real growth for 13 years now. 12 years ago, banks were plying customers with loans. Competition to buy second properties as investments was so competitive, properties could go in a day. But those days are long gone, because a recent report tells us that even buy to let is dying. Now landlords are having to drop rents or risk losing tenants. Kobus Lamprecht head of research at Rode and Associates says the percentage of flats standing empty in Cape Town surged from around 2% to over 8% at the beginning of this year. In Johannesburg it’s not as marked going from 3% to 7% The latest figures show that average rentals actually fell in both Limpopo, down by 4% and North West – down by 1%. If you want to live cheaply North West is your place – where you can rent for under R5000 per month. But then of course none of the municipalities in North West got a clean audit so you might not get water and electricity and still pay rates through the nose. So, what is going on with property. Should you just sell your home, rent, and take the rest of your money offshore. That is what some people are doing. They have downsized and are investing all their remaining funds offshore. Many others are emigrating. Consider this- according to the latest wealth report, three thousand-dollar millionaires, left South Africa recently. That just wiped out R45 billion rand from the economy. No wonder there is a glut of houses on the market. Estate Agents will always talk up the market, but what does the data tell us? To answer that question, we approached Lightstone. They analyse housing data down to the latest prices paid per suburb and they can show you exactly what is going on in the market. Take a look at their graphs and all the lines are going downhill. Even in Cape Town that enjoyed 12% inflation on house prices – the trends are the same. It sounds counter intuitive to talk about house price inflation- but the higher the number the better for you as a seller, so for example- if you had bought in the Cape in the early 2000’s and sold in 2014 you would have made a killing. Not anymore. R15 million-rand homes are just not selling as foreigners exit the market, transfer costs strangle sales and visa regulations make it difficult for foreigners to enter and exit the market. Take the transfer duty of 13% on a R10 million-rand home – just like that you have added another R130 000000 to the price tag. So, is there anywhere in South Africa where the property market can work for you? Yes, but it may not be what you want to hear. Lightstone’s graphs show an incredible return for properties under a million rand. Say to investors they should put their money into Hillbrow or Johannesburg’s inner city and they will fall about laughing. But that is where you might just get the best returns, either that or Umhlanga and Durban that has been showing the best returns. So much so that a big home with a sea view on the South Coast won’t sell for much more than R1.5 million in Leisure Bay. That same home in Umhlanga will net you R5 million. But sorry for you if you bought land on the South Coast at R400 000 now says the agent I won’t even be able to get you R150 000. In a light hearted but informative insert – we speak to the winners and the losers in the property market and tell you how best to navigate a difficult market, using the best and latest research.
